title: PermissionFile
description: Permission file that can define a default permission, a set of permissions or a list of inlined permissions.

default.description: The default permission set for the plugin

set.description: A list of permissions sets defined

DefaultPermission.description:
The default permission set of the plugin.

Works similarly to a permission with the "default" identifier.

description.description: Human-readable description of what the permission does. Tauri convention is to use `<h4>` headings in markdown content for Tauri documentation generation purposes.

PermissionSet.description: A set of direct permissions grouped together under a new name.

identifier.description: A unique identifier for the permission.

description.description: Human-readable description of what the permission does.

Permission.description:
Descriptions of explicit privileges of commands.

It can enable commands to be accessible in the frontend of the application.

If the scope is defined it can be used to fine grain control the access of individual or multiple commands.

identifier.description: A unique identifier for the permission.

description.description: Human-readable description of what the permission does. Tauri internal convention is to use `<h4>` headings in markdown content for Tauri documentation generation purposes.

commands.description: Allowed or denied commands when using this permission.

scope.description: Allowed or denied scoped when using this permission.

platforms.description: Target platforms this permission applies. By default all platforms are affected by this permission.

Commands.description:
Allowed and denied commands inside a permission.

If two commands clash inside of `allow` and `deny`, it should be denied by default.

Scopes.description:
An argument for fine grained behavior control of Tauri commands.

It can be of any serde serializable type and is used to allow or prevent certain actions inside a Tauri command. The configured scope is passed to the command and will be enforced by the command implementation.

## Example

```json { "allow": [{ "path": "$HOME/**" }], "deny": [{ "path": "$HOME/secret.txt" }] } ```

allow.description: Data that defines what is allowed by the scope.

deny.description: Data that defines what is denied by the scope. This should be prioritized by validation logic.

anyOf.description: Represents a map of [`String`] keys to [`Value`]s.

oneOf.description:
Everything a shell's UI needs: the saved servers (`servers`, `add_server`, `confirm_server`,
`remove_server`, `server_info`, `set_active`), sign-in (`sign_in`, `pair`, `sign_in_door`,
`sign_in_door_set_password`, `pair_confirm`, `pair_decline`), sign-out and the device list
(`sign_out`, `devices`, `revoke_device`), `open` (a server's page in the calling window, signed
in) and `notify` (a notification and the app badge). Every window gets every event
(`sew-app://servers`, `signed_out`, `warning`, `deep_link`, `pair_request`, `pair_refused`).
Not in it: `handoff`, which answers a code for the page's cookie (`sew-app:handoff`); the API
transport for a bundled UI (`api`, `gateway_open`, `gateway_send`, `gateway_close`,
`upload_bytes`: `sew-app:transport`); and `upload_file`, which reads a file the page names
(`sew-app:upload-file`).

#### This default permission set includes:

- `allow-servers`
- `allow-add-server`
- `allow-confirm-server`
- `allow-remove-server`
- `allow-server-info`
- `allow-set-active`
- `allow-sign-in`
- `allow-pair`
- `allow-sign-in-door`
- `allow-sign-in-door-set-password`
- `allow-pair-confirm`
- `allow-pair-decline`
- `allow-sign-out`
- `allow-devices`
- `allow-revoke-device`
- `allow-open`
- `allow-notify`

oneOf.description:
`handoff`: a single-use 60 s code that the calling page trades for the App's cookie session
(`POST /sew/native/handoff/redeem`). The plugin answers it only to a page on the account's own
server. Grant it only to the remote capability of the App's own site, never to a window that
loads other pages.

#### This permission set includes:

- `allow-handoff`

oneOf.description:
The API transport, for an App's bundled UI: `api` (the App's client API through the server's
native lane, with the device bearer kept in the app), `gateway_open`, `gateway_send` and
`gateway_close` (the gateway socket held in the app and relayed over a channel, its ticket put in
by the app), and `upload_bytes` (raw bytes to an upload or an image route). The page never gets
the bearer or a ticket. Grant it to the bundled UI's own capability; a server's live site has its
cookie session and doesn't need it. The `sewfile:` scheme needs no permission: it answers only
the bundled UI's pages.

#### This permission set includes:

- `allow-api`
- `allow-gateway-open`
- `allow-gateway-send`
- `allow-gateway-close`
- `allow-upload-bytes`

oneOf.description:
`upload_file`: the app reads a file at a path the page names and posts its bytes to an upload
or an image route. The page can name any file the app may read, so grant it only to a bundled UI
that takes the path from the person's own pick (a file dialog), never to a window that loads
other pages.

#### This permission set includes:

- `allow-upload-file`
